transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO - Emerald), Mina Alvarez (Lead ML Eng - Emerald), Samir Khan (Infra), Leah Park (PM)

Summary (auto):
Short discovery exploring model choices for Emerald's multilingual customer support assistant. Discussed context length needs (60k? 32k? shorter), hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) tradeoffs, KMS and audit requirements, tool-calling for knowledge base and back-end actions. Agreed next steps for security docs and a deep technical benchmark.

Topics:
- current stack and constraints
- estimated QPS / latency targets
- context window and retrieval approach
- multilingual quality and evals
- tool-calling (DB, ticket system, api exec)
- deployment options (hosted / dedicated / private VPC)
- security & compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs)

Transcript body:
00:00:02 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, today's the discovery for Emerald's customer assistant.. I'm Alex from Redwood, my colleague Priya is the SE who will dig into the latency / perf bits. Do you want to quickly intro from Emerald?
00:00:12 Jordan Lee: Yeah, Jordan here. CTO. We run multiregional SaaS for enterprise retail clients. Main ask is we want to build a high-accuracy multilingual assistant that can do context-aware responses and also execute tools - like open tickets, pull order info, run returns.
00:00:23 Mina Alvarez: Mina, lead on the ML side. We currently use a hybrid pipeline: light LLM for classification and retrieval for long context, but we want fewer hops and better in-prompt tool orchestration.
00:00:35 Samir Khan: Samir, infra. We're sensitive about data residency; some customers require EU-only storage and strict KMS controls. We also have peak traffic patterns with short spikes.
00:00:45 Leah Park: Leah here, PM; timeline is pilot in Q4 and production early Q1. Success metrics are latency under 300ms for short queries, under 1.2s for tool-assisted ops, and >85% multilingual NLU accuracy across EN/FR/ES/DE/JA.
00:01:00 Priya Patel: Great, appreciate that context. A few questions up front—what's your current retrieval architecture and average context sizes for the conversations you want to preserve?
00:01:12 Mina Alvarez: We keep a few KB articles + last 10 messages, typically ~3-4k tokens. But for complex ecommerce disputes we want to include order history and full chat transcripts, which can go to 40k tokens. Ideally we'd like support up to 64k for some cases.
00:01:30 Daniel Cho: (interject) 64k will push memory and throughput—depending on model it'll affect latency and cost a lot. But there are ways: chunking plus coarse retrieval or prefix KV caching.
00:01:45 Jordan Lee: We're leaning toward using open models to avoid vendor lock and cost, but need to evaluate quality and first-token latency across options.
00:01:55 Alex Morgan: Totally. We typically compare a few classes: smaller efficient open models (faster, cheaper, shorter context), medium LLMs with 32k support, and large long-context variants. For Emerald, given 64k occasional needs, we should consider a 32k+ approach with retrieval backstops unless you want to run dedicated long-context models for specific flows.
00:02:12 Mina Alvarez: Can Redwood host custom quantized models? We prefer 4-bit/8-bit quant for cost but worried about accuracy drop.
00:02:20 Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood Dedicated and Private both support quantized model variants and quant-aware kernels. For hosted, we also expose several quantized open model builds that we've validated — note some task-dependent degredation occurs, and we'll show you eval numbers.
00:02:34 Mina Alvarez: (pause) you said kernels—can you expand on that?
00:02:38 Priya Patel: Sure. Our runtime selects kernels per-operator based on architecture and sequence length. For certain quantization layouts we route through optimized kernels to keep latency acceptable. There's also continuous batching and KV prefix cache to amortize cost for repeated context.
00:02:54 Samir Khan: How about VPC/private deployments? We have strict data residency and some customers demand air-gapped options.
00:03:02 Alex Morgan: Private deployments offer customer-managed control plane and VPC peering. You can run Redwood Private within your cloud region or even on-prem for air-gapped needs. We integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs and retention controls.
00:03:16 Jordan Lee: SOC2? We need the vendor SOC2 summary for procurement.
00:03:19 Alex Morgan: Absolutely — I'll send the SOC2 Type II report and security whitepaper after this call.
00:03:25 Leah Park: For tool-calling: we want the assistant to call a ticketing API, look up orders, and also run a small JS snippet for price calc behind a permissions boundary. Is that supported?
00:03:36 Priya Patel: Yes. We have built-in function/tool calling primitives in the hosted API and Private will let you run custom connectors in your VPC. You can restrict which tools are callable by role, and audit each call. For code execution we recommend a sandboxed microservice with RBAC; Redwood can orchestrate the call but we don't run arbitrary customer code in the hosted plane.
00:03:54 Mina Alvarez: What's the overhead for function calls on latency? If the model calls a tool, do we pay double tokens?
00:04:00 Daniel Cho: There's typically an extra roundtrip: model outputs a function call, Redwood invokes the tool connector (fast if local VPC), then model consumes the result and replies. You pay for the tokens for the model generations and the additional request. In Dedicated/Private with local connectors the network overhead is small; hosted has slightly higher egress.
00:04:18 Jordan Lee: On the model side, any recommended open models for multilingual QA + tool-calls? We're evaluating LlamaX-32k, Mosaic-Large-30k, and Falcon-40b variants.
00:04:28 Priya Patel: We see good multilingual base quality from a couple of families. For tool-calling reliability and instruction-following, some of the LlamaX derivatives have strong performance; Falcon variants are faster on some hardware. LlamaX-32k is strong if you need high completion fidelity at longer context; Falcon is better latency/cost on shorter contexts. We can run a small eval on your prompts.
00:04:46 Mina Alvarez: Would a 32k model with retrieval be simpler than trying to run a 64k native model? We want consistency in the user experience.
00:04:53 Priya Patel: Often it's simpler to do hybrid: 32k model + retrieval stack + prefix KV caching for immediate history. The tradeoff is complexity in retrieval engineering vs the single-model long context approach, which increases GPU VRAM needs and cost.
00:05:10 Samir Khan: Price sensitivity is real — we need predictable unit costs. How does Redwood handle batching and pricing?
00:05:17 Alex Morgan: For hosted API, pricing is usage-based per token. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching settings and quant profiles to lower unit costs. For predictable budgets, Redwood Dedicated offers reserved capacity and flat monthly commitments with burst policies. Private is licensed; you pay for infra + platform.
00:05:32 Leah Park: If we go dedicated, can we reserve GPUs for peaks and autoscale?
00:05:37 Priya Patel: Yes, dedicated pools let you set autoscale thresholds and burst capacity to handle spikes. You can also define routing policies to fallback to other regions or cheaper model tiers if capacity is constrained.
00:05:47 Mina Alvarez: Regarding evals: can Redwood run metadata-level evals across languages, and show token-level latency and cost breakdowns per prompt?
00:05:55 Daniel Cho: Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency, per-route dashboards, and you can hook in your eval sets. We'll produce side-by-side model comparisons on your prompt set.
00:06:06 Jordan Lee: Ok, procurement questions — SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs?
00:06:10 Alex Morgan: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles, and detailed audit logs with retention controls. In Private you can route logs to your SIEM.
00:06:19 Samir Khan: KMS integration for keys? Customer-managed keys?
00:06:22 Alex Morgan: Yes, integrate with your KMS/HSM. For Private you can use customer-managed keys; for Hosted we support KMS integrations for encryption at rest and key wrapping.
00:06:31 Mina Alvarez: Perf question: for the 40k contexts we mentioned, what latency numbers should we expect?
00:06:36 Priya Patel: It depends on model and hardware. For a long-context 32-40k run on a large A100-class setup, first-token latencies can be in the 700ms-1.5s range; throughput per GPU falls with longer sequences. That's why we recommend retrieval-first for user-visible interactions and reserve long-context native runs for batch or critical escalations.
00:06:56 Jordan Lee: Can we do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model if the long model fails?
00:07:02 Alex Morgan: Yes, Redwood supports rollout policies, canary, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency/cost/region).
00:07:10 Leah Park: For the pilot, our plan is to do hosted for speed, with a Dedicated pilot for high-volume EU customers. Does that sound reasonable?
00:07:18 Priya Patel: That's a common pattern — hosted to iterate quickly, then shift critical workloads to dedicated or private for isolation and predictable cost.
00:07:25 Mina Alvarez: About model fine-tuning / instruction tuning — can Redwood manage model versioning and rollbacks?
00:07:31 Daniel Cho: Yes, model lifecycle management is part of the platform — pinning versions, rollouts, and automatic fallbacks. We also integrate tooling for eval regressions so you can detect quality drops post-rollout.
00:07:42 Samir Khan: For the tool connectors in Private, do you have reference connectors for Zendesk and our internal ticketing system?
00:07:48 Priya Patel: We have sample connectors for Zendesk, Salesforce, and common ticket systems; for proprietary systems we provide a connector SDK and can co-build if needed.
00:07:58 Jordan Lee: Any known gotchas migrating from our current pipeline? We have existing retrieval, RAG flows, and a homegrown orchestrator.
00:08:03 Alex Morgan: Migration often involves mapping intents, rewriting some prompts, and hooking your retrieval. The main ops work is around keys, VPC peering, and testing the fallback paths. Redwood has migration playbooks and a solutions engineering engagement option.
00:08:18 Mina Alvarez: Let's talk a bit about multilingual evals — we need 85%+ across five languages. How granular are the console metrics?
00:08:26 Daniel Cho: You can upload labeled evals per language and get per-prompt pass/fail, token-level cost, and diff across model versions. We'll export CSVs for your analysis.
00:08:36 Leah Park: How long for a benchmark run? We need a quick decision for pilot next week.
00:08:40 Priya Patel: For an initial smoke test across 1k prompts across languages, we can run 48-72 hours depending on queue and if you want Dedicated hardware reservations. For a thorough eval (10k prompts) maybe a week.
00:08:53 Jordan Lee: Are there limitations on function/tool calling frequency per session? Our design might have multiple tool calls per user request.
00:08:59 Alex Morgan: No hard limit — you configure rate limits and quotas. For hosted there are default rate limits; we can set customer-level quotas for production. For Private and Dedicated you control the limits.
00:09:10 Mina Alvarez: For tokenization differences across models, will that affect cost comparability?
00:09:15 Daniel Cho: Yes — tokenization varies, so we normalize cost per output and provide tokenization-adjusted comparisons in the console.
00:09:23 Jordan Lee: On the legal side, we'll need standard DPA and data processing addenda.
00:09:27 Alex Morgan: We'll include the DPA in the docs we send.
00:09:31 Leah Park: Any client references in retail who run similar multilingual tool-enabled assistants?
00:09:36 Alex Morgan: We have customers in retail and payments who run multi-region assistants — I'll share anonymized case studies with performance numbers.
00:09:43 Mina Alvarez: Ok, I want to call out one specific flow: dispute resolution where we need a 60k context of order + legal notes; it needs high fidelity and traceable tool calls. Potentially that should be dedicated?
00:09:55 Priya Patel: For legal/traceability, Dedicated or Private is better — gives you audit logs, isolated keys, and enforceable RBAC for tool calls. For pilot you could run a hosted smoke test but plan Dedicated for production.
00:10:07 Jordan Lee: If we start with hosted for feature testing, will we be penalized for later moving to Dedicated?
00:10:12 Alex Morgan: No vendor lock — the API is consistent across modes so migration is designed to be straightforward. We can help with a migration plan.
00:10:20 Leah Park: Let's recap and next steps.
00:10:23 Alex Morgan: Recap: Redwood will send SOC2 + security paper, hosted vs dedicated pricing, sample benchmarking plan. Priya will propose a tech deep dive concentrating on latency tests and VPC connector design. Mina will share prompt set and evaluation goals; Samir to share infra diagram. We'll target the technical deep dive next week.
00:10:41 Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Quick question — when you talk about routing policies, can we route by tenant or SLA?
00:10:46 Priya Patel: Yes you can route by policy including tenant tag, latency SLO, or cost. You can use fallback tiers per-tenant.
00:10:53 Mina Alvarez: One more nit — sometimes Redwood docs mention KV "cash" in the transcript — is that the same as KV cache?
00:10:58 Daniel Cho: (laughs) Yes, KV cache — sorry the auto-transcript sometimes fouls the spelling.
00:11:04 Leah Park: Any blockers for next week's pilot?
00:11:07 Samir Khan: None on our side, just need the security docs and the infra diagram.
00:11:11 Alex Morgan: We'll get those over. Thanks everyone.
00:11:15 Jordan Lee: Thanks.
